analysis.title: Silver's $55 Moment Of Truth Shorts, Selling And Soaring Skew
key_insights: Silver is trading around $55, described as the make-or-break level. Momentum is poor, and a break below could trigger an aggressive move lower with little meaningful support beneath.
Managed Money sold another $565 million in silver futures during October 6-13, the third consecutive week of selling. Cumulative selling has reached $2.2 billion.
Of the latest $565 million in selling, $160 million was long liquidation and $405 million was fresh shorts.

Silver futures aggregate open interest rose $1.6 billion, with much of the increase during the heaviest selling session. Combined with falling prices, this points to new short positions rather than longs exiting.

Silver is struggling against the dollar backdrop. The dollar gained 0.3% while December silver futures lost 3.4% during October 6-13. The dollar then retraced 0.5% and silver fell another 2.6%, so dollar weakness alone no longer revives the silver trade.
Industrial demand proxies are weak during October 6-13: US solar equities fell 4.7%, Chinese solar fell 1.6% and data center stocks fell 7.9%.

Silver's normalized 25-delta put-call skew briefly reached the 98th percentile of its one-year range, showing increasingly aggressive demand for downside protection that matches the bearish futures positioning.
risk_factors: A break below $55 in silver could trigger an aggressive move lower with little support beneath.
Silver is not responding to dollar weakness.
Weakness in solar and data center equities signals a weaker industrial demand backdrop for silver.
